children: Japanese rubber futures rose on Thursday, supported by a weaker yen and firmer Tokyo equities, though lower oil prices limited the advance.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was up 3.6 yen, or 0.85%, at 428.8 yen ($2.75) per kg, as of 0211 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 55 yuan, or 0.29%, to 18,900 yuan ($2,816.31) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) fell 45 yuan, or 0.3%, to 14,845 yuan per ton.
hovered near a two-week low as markets awaited the Bank of Japan's decision on Friday.
A weaker Japanese currency makes yen-denominated assets more affordable to overseas buyers.

Shares edged up in Asia on Thursday as investors bet the Federal Reserve is finally getting the jump on inflation, delivering its first rate hike in more than three years and calming a global bond selloff that had sent long-term yields soaring. Japan's Nikkei
Oil prices fell in early trade, extending the previous day's losses, as reports of Saudi Arabia offering extra crude cargoes through Oman reduced fears of supply disruptions in the Middle East.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for December delivery (STFZ6) last traded at 236.9 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.2%.
